item.title: Gemini Free Hyphenator
item.description:
Hyphenate Sanskrit Markdown outside of मूलम्.* details blocks (when doubtful readings also need fixing) using the llm/gemini path with the AI-prompt/Sanskrit_devanAgarI_markdown.md prompt — it carries the same split rules (insert a space at separable word boundaries and a hyphen inside compounds without reverting sandhi), preserves <details><summary>मूलम्</summary> blocks untouched, and lets the model also suggest corrections to doubtful text:

1

library.apply_function(fn=gemini.process_text_chunks_with_keys, dir_path=..., prompt=llm.get_prompt("~/gitland/sanskrit/sanskrit.github.io/content/groups/dyuganga/projects/text/proofreading/editing/AI-prompt/Sanskrit_devanAgarI_markdown.md"), dry_run=False)

followed by

1

library.apply_function(fn=MdFile.transform, dir_path="...", content_transformer=lambda x, *args, **kwargs: ocr_helper.fix_gemini_errors(x), dry_run=False)

Final Report

Report what was hyphenated, and flag anything left ambiguous for a human by inserting [[??]].

item.title: Hyphenator
item.description:
Hyphenate Sanskrit Markdown outside of मूलम्.* details blocks:
insert a space at word boundaries and a hyphen inside compounds, but only at boundaries that are separable.

Never revert sandhi — split the result of the sandhi, do not undo it. Non-separable mergers (dIrgha, guNa, vRddhi — dharmArtha, mahotsava, sadaiva) must stay joined, even inside a samAsa.

More rules are in the AI prompt.

Final Report

item.title: Interleaver
item.description:
Interleave translations or commentaries into the Markdown files you are given.

  1. Generate mUlam blocks if missing. If the files have no <details><summary>मूलम्</summary> blocks, create them first:

    1

    library.apply_function(fn=MdFile.transform, dir_path=dir_path, content_transformer=lambda c, *args, **kwargs: maker.generic_sanskrit_vipra_mUla(c))

    (maker is doc_curation.md.content_processor.details.maker.)

  2. Sanskrit commentaries (ṭīkā). If you are interleaving a commentary, call:

    1

    interleaver.interleave_TIkA_below_mUla(dest_file, commentary_file)

    (interleaver is doc_curation.md.content_processor.commentary.interleaver.)

  3. Otherwise (translations above mUlam). Follow the instructions in ~/gitland/sanskrit/sanskrit.github.io/content/groups/dyuganga/projects/text/proofreading/editing/AI-prompt/interleave-translation/mUla_and_En_translation/Insert_above_mUla.md — insert each translated segment directly above its corresponding <details><summary>मूलम्</summary> block, preserving the original Sanskrit text verbatim.

item.title: Local Hyphenator
item.description:
Hyphenate Sanskrit Markdown outside of मूलम्.* details blocks:
insert a space at word boundaries and a hyphen inside compounds, but only at boundaries that are separable.

Never revert sandhi — split the result of the sandhi, do not undo it. Non-separable mergers (dIrgha, guNa, vRddhi — dharmArtha, mahotsava, sadaiva) must stay joined, even inside a samAsa.

Local hyphenation

1

from doc_curation.sanskrit.hyphenator import hyphene

hyphene(text) implements those rules without an LLM: a space for word joints, a hyphen for samAsa joints. Apply it to prose blocks only — not headings, frontmatter, or <details><summary>मूलम्</summary> content — via MdFile.transform with a content_transformer (eg. details.helper.transform_details_with_soup), or library.apply_function over a directory.

item.title: OpenCode global instructions
item.description:
Global instructions

Subagents

  • Delegate to subagents whenever possible — exploration, research, multi-step work, or anything matching a listed agent’s description — to keep the main context small.
  • When running in JetBrains Air (which does not render background wakeups after a turn ends), poll active subagents periodically within the turn (using synchronous waits and manage_subagents checks) rather than ending the turn, and resume polling after handling any new user messages while subagents remain active.

Model selection

  • Be careful to use a free/lightweight model whenever possible.
  • OpenCode: For bulk, mechanical, or low-risk work (formatting, repetitive edits, simple searches, large-file scanning, TUI delegation), prefer a zero-cost OpenCode Go model such as opencode-go/beam-free or opencode-go/iceman-contributor-free (and opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash for reviewer). When delegating to a subagent, pass the model explicitly via the model parameter, e.g. opencode-go/beam-free#xhigh.
  • Antigravity: When delegating via invoke_subagent, prefer lighter model tiers (Model: "flash_lite" or Model: "flash") for bulk, mechanical, or low-risk work, and reserve "pro" or "inherit" for judgment calls and verification.
  • Reserve stronger/paid models for judgment calls, verification of free/lighter-model output, and tasks where the lighter model is unsuitable.

Compute

  • Do NOT run CPU-heavy tasks on the local machine; offload them to Kaggle or Google Colab instead. Avoid grinding the local CPU.

Existing code

Use and maintain existing code where possible — it is installed in the venv at ~/gitland/python_venv, so invoke ~/gitland/python_venv/bin/python (not the default python3).

item.title: PDF to Markdown
item.description:
Convert the PDF you are given to Markdown. Work in this order and skip a step when it is unnecessary.

  1. Text layer first. Check the file with pdfinfo, then extract with pdftotext. If it yields clean prose in the right script, skip OCR.

  2. OCR only when extraction is garbage, or is helpful to decypher it — no text layer, mojibake, one word per line, wrong script, or page after page of ...[[??]]. (See the global instructions for preferences/ subagents).

item.title: Proofreader
item.description:
Proofread and edit the Markdown files you are given (possibly with the aid of parallel scan pdf etc.).

Text Cleanup and Normalization

  • Remove hard-wrapped line breaks to create continuous paragraphs.
  • Correct obvious typographical errors (e.g., a space in the middle of a word).
  • Remove wasteful newlines, like ones before </details>, between half-verses…
  • Preserve intentional styles like bold and italic.
  • Preserve existing headings and paragraphs; edit only what was asked.

Source Error Handling

  • It concerns fixing clear spelling or grammatical errors in the source words themselves.
  • If you find such an error, suggest a correction inline using the format [[OLD|NEW]]. Example: [[prarabvaṁ|prārabdhaṁ]].
  • Never guess at illegible text: mark the smallest span (e.g. …[[??]]) and move on.
  • Check [[Pnnn]] page markers against the printed folio (if provided) — PDF/book offsets drift between volumes and even within one volume.

Final Markdown Formatting

  • Quotes & Mantras: Enclose short quotes (under 5 words) in " and format longer quotes or mantras as blockquotes (>).
  • Structure: End verse lines with two spaces for a soft break. Separate paragraphs with a blank line.
  • Page Numbers: Format page numbers (e.g., ६४) as [[P64]] at the precise point of the page break. This can be within a paragraph which continues to the next page.
  • Footnotes: Format footnotes (e.g., *) using Markdown’s footnote syntax ([^1]). Place the definition at the end. Make the footnote definitions appear next to the paragraph containing the corresponding footnote reference. Ensure that footnote references are unique, reflecting the number used in the source whenever possible. For example if footnote named 1 appears in page 12, make the reference 12_1.

Hyphenation

  • When the text is Sanskrit, hand it to the hyphenator subagent once your edits are settled.

Report

  • Report the changes made, and list anything left for a human — doubtful readings, missing source images, or style rules that did not apply.

item.title: Reviewer
item.description:
Review the current changes. List findings in severity order with file and line references.

Rules -

  • Functions should not be too big - Severity increases every 100 lines. Split into smaller functions.
  • Modules should not be too big - Severity increases every 10 functions. Convert into package with multiple modules.
  • Any significantly large data should be externalized into TOML files and such.

item.title: Tesseract OCR
item.description:
Run Tesseract OCR and other bulk batch jobs on Kaggle or Colab, never on the local machine. Keep run scripts, dataset staging and a short README in the project.

  • Keep run scripts, dataset staging and a short README with kernel/dataset IDs and commands in the project, not only in /tmp — /tmp is wiped on session restart.
  • Install dependencies inside every run: poppler-utils for pdf2image, and language data via tessdata_best/<lang>.traineddata when apt lacks it (e.g. tesseract-ocr-san); confirm with tesseract --list-langs.
  • Run Tesseract sequentially. On a 4-vCPU Kaggle box, 4 workers turn a 7 s page into a >120 s timeout — parallelism is a pessimisation for OCR.
  • Wrap each page in subprocess.run(..., timeout=…) and write its output immediately, so one pathological scan cannot hang the session and partial results survive.
  • Kaggle publishes no logs or outputs until a kernel finishes, so RUNNING says nothing about progress. Prefer several short, targeted runs over one long one, and print per-chunk progress lines.
  • If a bulk job stalls twice, stop retrying. Count exactly which pages are actually needed and OCR only those.
